title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Printing and Distributing the Court Criminal Procedure Document Formats (Sample)
full_text_en:
Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Style of Court Criminal Litigation Documents (Sample)

Fa Fa [1999] No. 12

All local people's courts at various levels nationwide, all military courts, all railway transportation intermediate courts and basic people's courts, all maritime courts, and all courts of Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

On April 6, 1999, the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, at its 1051st session, discussed and adopted the Style of Court Criminal Litigation Documents (Sample). This is an important measure taken by the Supreme People's Court to fully implement the Criminal Procedure Law and the Criminal Law, vigorously promote the adversarial trial mode, reform the preparation of litigation documents, and improve the quality of litigation documents.

Litigation documents, especially adjudicative documents, prepared by the people's courts are the embodiment of the people's courts' exercise of the state's judicial power, are legally binding legal instruments, and are the ultimate vehicle of judicial justice. They concern the correct implementation of national laws and regulations, the protection of the parties' litigation rights and lawful interests, and also the impartial image of the people's courts in seeking truth from facts, handling cases according to law, enforcing the law impartially, and being upright and incorruptible.

The preparation of adjudicative documents is an important part of trial work, an important task for judges, and a basic construction of the court's trial business. Leaders of courts at all levels and the vast number of judges must fully understand the significance of preparing good adjudicative documents, adopt effective measures in a reform-oriented spirit, and strive to improve the quality of adjudicative documents. The idea that "as long as the case is handled properly, it is fine, and it does not matter whether the adjudicative document is well-written or not" is extremely erroneous and harmful.

Since the Supreme People's Court issued the Style of Court Litigation Documents (Trial) in June 1992, various localities have taken measures to actively explore the rules for preparing adjudicative documents, and a number of excellent adjudicative documents have emerged. However, overall, the current level of preparation is not high, mainly because adjudicative documents are uniform in form, lack authentication and reasoning, do not show the formation process of the judgment result, and lack persuasive force. In response to this situation, the National Conference of Presidents of High People's Courts held at the end of last year emphasized the need to accelerate the pace of reform of adjudicative documents, "making adjudicative documents impeccable, so that adjudicative documents become a vehicle for displaying the court's civilized and impartial judicial image to the public, and truly possess judicial authority."

In order to sum up experience and further improve the quality of litigation documents, the Supreme People's Court decided to comprehensively revise the Style of Court Litigation Documents (Trial) issued in 1992. To coordinate with the implementation of the amended Criminal Procedure Law and the Criminal Law, it decided to first revise the criminal part of the document style. The focus of the revision is on the sections concerning facts (including evidence) and reasons. This is because current adjudicative documents have two major shortcomings. First, when stating the facts, they do not prove the crime, do not specify the specific evidence, but only use boilerplate phrases such as "the above criminal facts are confirmed by witness testimony, documentary evidence, and expert conclusions, and the defendant also confessed." Witness testimony: whose testimony, and what is its content? Documentary evidence: what is the documentary evidence, and what is its content? Expert conclusions: who made them, and what is their content? None of this is included. The judge's authentication and acceptance of evidence are not reflected in the adjudicative document. Second, there is no reasoning or insufficient reasoning; the reasoning section has no reasons, only citation of legal provisions; it does not explain the rationale for applying the law. Therefore, the persuasive force is also weak. The most exquisite part of an adjudicative document is the reasoning section, which best demonstrates the judge's skill. Therefore, when implementing the revised document style and reforming the preparation of litigation documents, the focus should be on making efforts in two areas: enhancing the analysis and authentication of evidence, and strengthening the reasoning of adjudicative documents.

The style sample is hereby printed and distributed to you (separately issued). Please organize trial personnel to study it and earnestly implement it. To this end, the following notice is given:

1. The reform of adjudicative documents shall be organically combined with the "Trial Quality Year" and the "Strive to Be a People-Satisfied Good Court, Strive to Be a People-Satisfied Good Judge" activities currently being carried out across the national court system. Improving the quality of adjudicative documents is an important part of improving the quality of trial work. Courts at all levels shall list the quality of litigation documents, especially adjudicative documents, as an important part of trial work quality, and shall list the preparation of adjudicative documents as an important standard for assessing judges' trial work ability, and shall implement it firmly and well, thereby promoting the in-depth development of the "Trial Quality Year" and the "Strive to Be a People-Satisfied Good Court, Strive to Be a People-Satisfied Good Judge" activities.

2. Organize study and strengthen training. Courts at all levels shall organize the vast number of judges to earnestly study the speeches of President Xiao Yang and Vice President Zhu Mingshan at the National Conference of Presidents of High People's Courts held at the end of last year, so as to enhance their awareness of reforming the preparation of adjudicative documents; and to earnestly study the revised document style and its explanations, so as to improve the level of preparation of adjudicative documents. Among the 164 proposed document styles, 53 are newly added based on the amended Criminal Procedure Law, the Criminal Law, and relevant judicial interpretations; most of the other document styles have been revised and supplemented to varying degrees on the basis of the original styles, and requirements have been put forward for the preparation of each type of document. When studying, attention shall be paid to summarizing the experience gained since the implementation of the trial style. To facilitate study and application in trial practice, the Supreme People's Court has printed the revised document style as a booklet for the study and work of judges engaged in criminal trial work.

While organizing judges to study, courts at all levels shall strengthen the training of judges. For a long time, we have not included the preparation of litigation documents in training content, thus it is a weak link. To improve the overall quality of the court contingent, the Supreme People's Court has decided to take three years to conduct a rotational training of all presidents, vice presidents, division chiefs, and deputy division chiefs of intermediate people's courts and above. High people's courts shall also promptly conduct rotational training of judges of basic people's courts and people's tribunals. At the same time, litigation document training courses shall be held, with the Supreme People's Court and high people's courts sharing the training tasks at different levels. The National Judges College shall be responsible for training high people's courts and the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, the presiding judges of intermediate people's courts in provincial capitals and cities with separate planning, the division chiefs and deputy division chiefs of the criminal divisions and the complaint and petition divisions, as well as the teachers of the spare-time college for judges; high people's courts and their spare-time college branches (or judge training centers) shall be responsible for organizing the training of their own judges and those of lower courts, as well as teachers; intermediate people's courts with the necessary conditions may also host litigation document training courses.

3. In order to promptly summarize and explore the experience of preparing adjudicative documents, various localities may exchange experiences through holding litigation document seminars, evaluation meetings, and other forms. The Supreme People's Court intends to hold a seminar on the reform of criminal adjudicative documents in n month of this year, and hopes that various localities will prepare and recommend a number of excellent criminal adjudicative documents. The Supreme People's Court intends to publicly publish a Selection of Excellent Criminal Adjudicative Document Examples to promote the development of the reform of adjudicative documents.

4. The Style of Court Criminal Litigation Documents (Sample) shall come into effect from July 1, 1999. The criminal part of the Style of Court Litigation Documents (Trial) issued by the General Office of our Court on June 20, 1992 shall be simultaneously abolished. If any opinions arise during implementation in various localities, please promptly report them to our Court.

April 30, 1999
